thread:
maya: heads-up — noticed some tenants still sending X-Client-Version: v1 after we flipped the redirect rule; hits are low but we saw a spike in 2 tenants. anyone tracking fallback quotas?
ajit: thanks, maya. which rule did we flip? the graceful-fallback toggle or the hard redirect?
maya: console toggle -> graceful-fallback enabled yesterday 09:12. policy should route v1 -> legacy pool but fallthrough to v2 when capacity allows. these tenants somehow hit the fallback path to v2 directly.
carla: hmm could be header collision + token affinity. are they using mixed clients from the same API key?
maya: yes, one tenant has both mobile (v1 SDK) and server (v2 SDK) sharing a key.
dani: that explains it — routing uses token hash first, then version tag. mixed clients break the deterministic affinity. we debated this in the routing RFC but opted for token-first to avoid tenant split.
kevin: quick thought: console could show a per-key warning and expose a per-key opt-out flag to preserve old affinity if user wants. not ideal but quick mitigation.
maya: console warning is good. also need to ensure telemetry sampling marks these as "mixed-client" to avoid polluting v2 quality metrics.
ajit: agree. current telemetry sampling only tags by route target, not by incoming client-version header. we need a small agent change to add a label.
dani: caution: sampling rates matter. if we tag all mixed-client hits, we'll bias our regression detector. suggest: label them AND set separate sampling bucket (0.5% by default) then ramp if we need more signal.
carla: we should also avoid sudden quota thrash. If we start sampling and then route more to v2 probes, quotas could overrun. propose a canary with static quota cap: probe <= 5 RPS per tenant.
kevin: implementation sketch:
```
when request:
  if header X-Client-Version == v1 and token seen-with-v2:
    mark tag: mixed_client=true
    route with policy: prefer legacy unless probe-window open
```
Probe-window controlled by console per-tenant (default off).
ajit: ops question — how do we surface this to SRE so they don't assume an incident when v2 chatter shows up?
ops-bot: deploy-notice: routing-agent v0.93 deployed to canary cluster at 4112345700, monitor prod-routes:v2-probe alert for 30m.
maya: thanks, bot. SRE — can we add a short runbook note: "mixed-client routing spikes expected when enabling per-tenant probe"?
kevin: I can add console copy and a tooltip explaining "If your app mixes v1/v2 SDKs on the same API key, enable per-key probe to safely test v2; otherwise keep graceful-fallback".
dani: also add a telemetry flag so regression jobs ignore mixed_client-tagged traffic unless explicitly included. we don't want false positives.
carla: timeline proposal: 0) add tag + 0.5% sample (devs only) 1) console warning + per-key opt-in 2) canary probe for 24h @5 RPS per tenant 3) decision to roll or pause.
ajit: sounds good. who owns tagging change?
maya: I'll pick up tagging + console warning copy. kevin can wire the per-key opt-in control. dani owns telemetry sampling config, carla owns SRE runbook update.
kevin: will open PR for UI toggle and API surface (PATCH /keys/:id/probe) after tagging PR lands.
dani: I'll add exclusion rules to regression jobs and create a separate alert dashboard for mixed_client traffic.
maya: perfect. let's try to keep the probe off by default. post back when PRs link. :thumbsup:
